chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Joe and Moses Garland's society gigs
summary: Garland's eight-piece band played lodge and fraternity dances, with Clyde Bernhardt on trombone singing one number a night.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah.
You weren't with any formal group.
That's right. I was gigging from then on. I was gigging with Joe Garland; you know, that's when I first started with Joe Garland, gigging with him.
Wasn't his brother Moses?
His brother, yeah. Well, they were both... It was Moses' band, supposedly. Joe had taken it over.
What did Moses play?

He had a trumpet. He was another Sy Oliver. In fact, I think he was better than Sy. He had a trumpet. He got the work. He had a lot of work. He was working four and five times a week sometimes, all during the week.
He had a lot of connections with lodges and clubs and things.
That's right. He had a lot of connections.
Weddings? Did you play weddings?
No. I don't ever do that. We played a lot
Holmes (12/5) - 45
of Society affairs and school things... Not school...
Colleges?
Well, I guess you would call them, like, the different societies. The Omega Phi Sci...
Oh, the fraternity houses.
Yeah. Those gigs. I don't mean that particular group, but I mean, that's what they were. We played a lot of them kind of gigs.
And what would your bands be? About five pieces?

Oh, no-no. We had at least eight pieces. Let me see, we had three saxophones sometimes, most of the time, and two trumpets and a trombone -- three brass and three saxophones. And a rhythm section. Sometimes we had three saxophones, three brass.
Do you remember who played trombone on those things? Was it Clyde?
Yeah, Clyde.
Clyde Bernhardt.
Clyde Bernhardt.
Was he singing in those days, or just playing trombone?
Joe would let him sing one number a night, and Clyde would have his book... He had his own music and everything. Joe didn't care if he didn't sing a lick! Yeah, he let him sing one number.
